Arizona State Sun Devils.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Arizona State Sun Devils.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Arizona State Sun Devils.play_caller: Marcus Arroyo, and the guide treats the arrangement as an open question. It records that Kenny Dillingham mostly called plays in 2024 and Arizona State averaged 6.1 yards per play; with Arroyo calling them last year that fell to 5.6.
Arizona State Sun Devils.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Arizona State Sun Devils.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Arizona State Sun Devils.qb_development: Addressed as an expectation attached to the head coach's reputation. The guide notes Dillingham once tried to recruit Cutter Boley to Oregon, which it reads as genuine belief, and contextualizes Boley's 15-to-12 touchdown-to-interception season at Kentucky by noting he had an unreliable supporting cast and no one of Dillingham's reputation.
Arizona State Sun Devils.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 12.
Arizona State Sun Devils.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Arizona State Sun Devils.prior_school: Oregon is raised as a recruiting connection for Dillingham and Boley. On the roster the guide records Cutter Boley from Kentucky, Reed Harris from Boston College, Owen Long from Colorado State and Ashton Stamps from LSU.
Arizona State Sun Devils.portal_recruiting: Notable transfers were added on the defensive line and at linebacker, with Colorado State's Owen Long singled out as someone who could turn heads at a higher level, and LSU's Ashton Stamps called a good addition at corner.
Arizona State Sun Devils.vsin_assessment: Expectations recalibrated, and one coaching arrangement questioned. The guide frames an 8-5 season feeling like a massive disappointment as outrageous given Arizona State went 3-9 in 2023, and attributes the shift to Dillingham reaching the playoff in his second year. Its stated criticism is not of the head coach but of the division of labour: with one of college football's brightest offensive minds on the sideline, fans will keep asking why he is not calling plays, especially after a year ranked 49th in Adjusted EPA per play at 0.01.
Arizona State Sun Devils.strengths: A head coach the guide calls one of college football's brightest offensive minds who has already delivered a playoff run, full coordinator continuity, and a portal class the guide rates on the defensive line and at linebacker.
Arizona State Sun Devils.concerns: The play-calling arrangement and the drop from 6.1 to 5.6 yards per play that came with it, the loss of Sam Leavitt following the earlier loss of Cam Skattebo, a secondary the guide identifies as the pressing need, significant roster turnover and a tough schedule.
Arizona State Sun Devils.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked judgement is that the odds are stacked against Dillingham, while noting he has been in that position before.

Arizona Wildcats.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Brent Brennan arriving after a successful run at San Jose State, following Jedd Fisch, and notes the late start left him no time to get things right.
Arizona Wildcats.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Arizona Wildcats.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Arizona Wildcats.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Arizona Wildcats.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Arizona Wildcats.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Arizona tying for seventh in Game on Paper's Adjusted EPA per play allowed at -0.14, driven by a third-ranked EPA per dropback allowed of -0.24.
Arizona Wildcats.qb_development: Addressed through a documented bounceback and an established relationship. The guide records Noah Fifita throwing for 3,228 yards with 29 touchdowns and six interceptions and finishing as PFF's 17th-ranked passer, a major recovery from a poor 2024, and credits an established rapport with returning coordinator Seth Doege.
Arizona Wildcats.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 14 returning starters — totalling 17, among the highest in the guide.
Arizona Wildcats.staff_turnover: Addressed retrospectively and favourably: the guide calls Brennan's staff changes a home run and says they leave him in good standing with the university.
Arizona Wildcats.portal_recruiting: Credited to the head coach directly — the guide calls his portal work strong and his recruiting instincts sound, and records that Brennan and Gonzales hit the portal hard for potential instant-impact starters in the secondary.
Arizona Wildcats.vsin_assessment: A recovery credited to the coach, with the ceiling questioned. The guide records Arizona falling to 4-8 in 2024 and putting Brennan on the hot seat, then answering with a 9-4 season it says was a couple of very close losses from something bigger. It calls his staff changes a home run. Its caution is stated as a warning against extrapolation: replicating or building on 2025 is the hope, but that is also what Tucson hoped for in 2024.
Arizona Wildcats.strengths: A Stability Score of 17 with head coach, both coordinators and the quarterback all returning; staff changes the guide calls a home run; a coordinator credited with excellent work on a defense that ranked among the best in EPA per dropback allowed; and 14 returning starters.
Arizona Wildcats.concerns: Four defensive backs lost to the NFL including a second-round pick and two all-conference selections on a unit the guide says was special specifically because it slowed the conference's most explosive passing games; three offensive line starters to replace; the quarterback's 2024 season and occasional injury trouble; and a schedule the guide says makes finishing above .500 in conference play a challenge.
Arizona Wildcats.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

BYU Cougars.dc: Kelly Poppinga, replacing Jay Hill, who left to join Kyle Whittingham at Michigan.
BYU Cougars.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
BYU Cougars.dc_status: New — the guide records Jay Hill's departure and Poppinga's promotion, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
BYU Cougars.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
BYU Cougars.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
BYU Cougars.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records BYU allowing 19.6 points per game or fewer in back-to-back seasons, giving up only 19.1 last year.
BYU Cougars.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy. The guide's quarterback diagnosis is that Bear Bachmeier was far more comfortable running than passing.
BYU Cougars.qb_development: Framed as a specific developmental target rather than a coaching record. The guide says becoming a more cerebral pocket passer with better accuracy is the next stage for Bachmeier and uses the PFF grades to make the point precisely — a 78.9 overall grade put him in the top 50, but his 77.0 rushing grade was what raised the profile, and if the passing grade surpasses the rushing grade BYU has something special.
BYU Cougars.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 3 for 13 returning starters, totalling 14.
BYU Cougars.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, where Jay Hill left for Michigan and Kelly Poppinga took over.
BYU Cougars.prior_school: Michigan is where Jay Hill went, to join Kyle Whittingham. On the roster the guide records Cade Uluave from Cal and Kyle Kasper from Oregon.
BYU Cougars.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect. The guide's retention point is about the head coach: his success drew Penn State, which it says was desperate for him, and BYU's boosters brought him back with what it describes as a bottomless pit of money.
BYU Cougars.vsin_assessment: Strong on the head coach, unresolved on the coordinator change. The guide records Kalani Sitake winning double-digit games in four of the last six seasons and says last year's team had a real case for the playoff field. On the defensive change its conclusion is deliberately unresolved: things should be fine given the playmakers scattered through the defense, but you never quite know.
BYU Cougars.strengths: A head coach with four double-digit-win seasons in six who was retained against a Power Four programme's pursuit, offensive-coordinator and quarterback continuity, nearly every impactful player back from a 12-win team, two straight seasons under 19.6 points allowed, and eight defenders who started games returning.
BYU Cougars.concerns: A new defensive coordinator taking over a unit that lost its architect to Michigan, a quarterback whose passing lags his running, and the loss of leading receiver Parker Kingston, who the guide records was expelled from school over off-field conduct, leaving heavy reliance on an unproven group.
BYU Cougars.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Baylor Bears.oc: Jake Spavital, whom the guide calls an elite play-caller.
Baylor Bears.dc: Joe Klanderman, in after six years at Kansas State.
Baylor Bears.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Baylor Bears.dc_status: New — the guide records Klanderman taking over, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Baylor Bears.play_caller: Changed on defense in a way the guide treats as significant: Dave Aranda has stopped calling the defense, which it calls a wise step aside despite his reputation as a defensive mind, with Klanderman taking over. Jake Spavital calls the offense.
Baylor Bears.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but characterised functionally: the guide describes a more quarterback-friendly offense known for receivers running free, in which deep-ball touch should produce big plays.
Baylor Bears.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but a stated preference is recorded: Klanderman has been open about wanting activity in the opposing backfield, so the guide expects plenty of blitzing.
Baylor Bears.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Baylor Bears.qb_development: Framed as the season's central coaching question. The guide asks whether Spavital can unlock DJ Lagway, records Lagway as the top-ranked quarterback in the 2024 class whose Florida season produced 14 interceptions and 19 sacks, credits accumulated injuries as a factor, and sees a major turnaround available conditional on the line — noting Sawyer Robertson put up big numbers in this system and rating Lagway arguably more talented.
Baylor Bears.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback both change, and the head coach has given up defensive play-calling. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 9.
Baylor Bears.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive side, but structurally significant because the head coach also handed over the play-calling.
Baylor Bears.prior_school: Kansas State for Klanderman. On the roster the guide records DJ Lagway from Florida.
Baylor Bears.portal_recruiting: Not addressed as a staff-driven effect. The guide records DJ Lagway as a high-profile addition at quarterback and agrees a change of scenery was needed for him.
Baylor Bears.vsin_assessment: Blunt about the record, hopeful about the changes. The guide records an excellent start — 2-7 in year one, then 12-2 and a Sugar Bowl win — then three losing seasons in the last four, and says it is honestly shocking Aranda still has his job. It rates the decision to hand over the defense a wise step aside, expects the defense to improve at all three levels, and says last year's 32.6 points allowed per game should come down considerably.
Baylor Bears.strengths: An elite play-caller on offense inheriting a unit that scored 31.1 points per game, a defensive coordinator with six years at Kansas State and a clear aggressive identity, a head coach willing to delegate his own specialty, a loaded defensive line, and a bigger and deeper offensive line.
Baylor Bears.concerns: Three losing seasons in four, an offensive line rebuilt around one returning starter, a quarterback coming off 14 interceptions and 19 sacks, and the guide's own note that heavy blitzing exposes the secondary more than usual.
Baylor Bears.betting: The guide states the stakes explicitly in market terms: with a tough schedule and a 5.5 win total, failure to cash the Over likely means Aranda is looking for a defensive coordinator job next year. Its supporting case is the talent to take a huge step forward on defense and excitement about Lagway in a more quarterback-friendly offense.

Cincinnati Bearcats.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Cincinnati Bearcats.dc_status: New — the guide records the Nate Woody hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Cincinnati Bearcats.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Cincinnati Bearcats.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Cincinnati ranking fifth nationally in Game on Paper's Adjusted EPA per play at 0.14 with Brendan Sorsby, and characterises his replacement JC French as an accurate passer who works underneath rather than a consistent deep-ball threat.
Cincinnati Bearcats.defensive_scheme: Named. The guide records some excitement around Woody's aggressive 3-4 and says he largely did well at Army.
Cincinnati Bearcats.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Cincinnati Bearcats.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 5 — one of the lowest in the guide.
Cincinnati Bearcats.staff_turnover: Both coordinator positions change per the Stability Score table, with the guide naming and crediting the defensive hire.
Cincinnati Bearcats.prior_school: Army for Woody. On the roster the guide records JC French from Georgia Southern and Jacob Finley, Jasper Beeler and Filip Maciorowski from Northern Illinois.
Cincinnati Bearcats.portal_recruiting: Credited alongside the coordinator hire: the guide says the Nate Woody hire and instant-impact transfers have meaningfully changed the defense, and records Cincinnati raiding Northern Illinois for three defenders.
Cincinnati Bearcats.vsin_assessment: Direct about the head coach. The guide notes Scott Satterfield has won seven or fewer games in six consecutive years, so his shine is wearing off if it has not already, making this a big season, and says he should really be on the hot seat. Its conditional chain is explicit: without an offense capable of generating explosive plays this becomes a long year, and a long year for Cincinnati could mean a short one for Satterfield.
Cincinnati Bearcats.strengths: A defensive coordinator hire the guide credits with meaningfully changing the unit, an aggressive 3-4 it expresses excitement about, an improved secondary through the portal, good size on the defensive line and a solid linebacking corps.
Cincinnati Bearcats.concerns: A Stability Score of 5 with both coordinators and the quarterback changing, only nine returning starters, the loss of Sorsby plus a 13-touchdown receiver and a tight end to the NFL, an underwhelming backfield and unproven receivers, and a head coach the guide says should be on the hot seat.
Cincinnati Bearcats.betting: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The coaching link runs both ways in the guide's argument: it credits the Woody hire and instant-impact transfers for the defense, while saying it is hard to imagine what the offense looks like without Sorsby. It singles out a 5 September loss to Boston College as the result that could send the season off the rails.

Colorado Buffaloes.oc: Brennan Marion, whose system worked at UNLV and Sacramento State.
Colorado Buffaloes.dc: Chris Marve, the former Virginia Tech coordinator.
Colorado Buffaloes.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Colorado Buffaloes.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Colorado Buffaloes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name beyond the coordinators.
Colorado Buffaloes.offensive_scheme: Named and described in detail. The guide calls it Marion's 'Go-Go' system, a fast-paced power rushing offense that uses multiple backs and relies on fresh legs to break long runs inside, with rushing success setting up deep shots as a spread variation. Its open question is whether it translates to this level, and its conclusion is conditional on the line: given strong play up front there is no reason it should not work.
Colorado Buffaloes.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Colorado Buffaloes.tempo: Stated as fast — the guide describes the Go-Go system as fast-paced.
Colorado Buffaloes.run_pass: Stated. The system is power rushing first, with rushing success setting up deep shots.
Colorado Buffaloes.personnel: Stated in part — the guide records that the scheme uses multiple backs and relies on fresh legs.
Colorado Buffaloes.qb_development: Addressed as a scheme fit rather than a coaching record. The guide expects Julian Lewis' rise to begin, notes he is a traditional pro-style passer who will improvise less than Shedeur Sanders did, and says he has the arm talent for the downfield throws Marion's system needs.
Colorado Buffaloes.continuity: Only the head coach returns. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 3 for 15 returning starters, totalling 7.
Colorado Buffaloes.staff_turnover: Significant and explicitly cited as a reason for change. The guide lists significant coaching staff changes among the reasons it expects a different 2026, alongside Deion Sanders doing much better with the health concerns that had made life difficult on and off the field.
Colorado Buffaloes.prior_school: UNLV and Sacramento State for Marion's system; Virginia Tech for Marve. On the roster the guide records Isaac Wilson from Utah.
Colorado Buffaloes.portal_recruiting: Credited as hard work bringing reliable contributors through the portal, with heavy defensive reinforcement — all-conference Group of Five performers at all three levels, plus corners from big-time programmes.
Colorado Buffaloes.vsin_assessment: Expecting a different year, with responsibility placed on the coaches. The guide cites the head coach's improved health, significant staff changes and strong portal work as its reasons. On defense it sets a top-25 finish as a realistic goal given Colorado ranked 13th in Adjusted EPA per play allowed at -0.13 in 2024 before regressing to 56th at -0.03, and places responsibility on Marve since the group does not lack playmakers.
Colorado Buffaloes.strengths: A named and well-defined offensive system with a track record at two previous stops, two potential pros at tackle plus a proven starter at center to run it, a heavily reinforced defense with all-conference Group of Five performers at all three levels, and a recent defensive benchmark of 13th nationally to aim back at.
Colorado Buffaloes.concerns: A Stability Score of 7 with both coordinators and the quarterback new, a scheme unproven at this level, a quarterback with parts of three games' experience, and a defense that regressed from 23.1 to 30.5 points allowed.
Colorado Buffaloes.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
